title: Friedman translation for propositional proofs

based_on.title: Friedman’s A-Translation (October 27, 1992)
based_on.pages: §4, printed pp.4–5: definition and Lemma6, propositional restriction

summary: Translate constructive proof trees relative to a formula parameter, retain every changed assumption, and distinguish atom renaming from general formula substitution.
abstract: A proof may use falsum to conclude any formula. Replacing falsum by an ordinary formula therefore seems to break the proof at once. Friedman translation makes the replacement work by adding the replacement as an alternative to every atomic statement. We construct a rule-by-rule transformation of supplied intuitionistic certificates and show exactly which assumptions change. Choosing falsum as the parameter recovers the original formulas up to constructive proof, while other parameters can change their meaning. Small countermodels distinguish this transformation from ordinary substitution and from the negative translation of classical proofs.
